title: If you can see the service, it's theatre
subtitle: The good version is nearly invisible. You just stop having to ask for things.

text: Anticipation costs crew. Performance only costs choreography.
sub: A line-up of staff applauding you up the gangway is free. A barman who has your coffee right on the second morning is a staffing model, and it shows up in the fare.

items.head: Enough crew per guest
items.body: Nobody notices where you like to sit while covering forty other cabins. Attention is arithmetic before it is attitude.

items.head: Crew who come back
items.body: Long contracts and low turnover mean the person who learned you in April is still aboard in October. Ask about tenure.

items.head: Permission to decide
items.body: The best crew fix things without asking a supervisor. Where every kindness needs approval, you get apology, not remedy.

quote: The finest service I've had at sea I only noticed later — going back over the week and finding nothing I'd asked for twice.

text: Weigh crew ratio and crew tenure. Ignore the choreography.
sub: Two numbers and one question — how many crew, how long do they stay, and are they trusted to act. They predict a week at sea better than any photograph of a suite ever has.

title: Send this to whoever you'd share a cabin with
body: And if you want the unglamorous version, DM me the word CREW and I'll send the questions I actually put to a line before I recommend it.
